evidence: DESIGN ANALYSIS (no inversion found). (1) Aggregation is monotone non-decreasing in every dimension: tests/scoring.toml lines 1-11 gates render/constraints = 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floors functional = 0.05; tests/tools/score.py line 41 gates_passed = all(score > 0.0), line 46 weighted = positive linear sum, line 47 floors_passed requires functional > 0.05, line 48 reward = weighted only if gates and floors pass, else 0.0. Raising any dimension score never lowers reward; the gate/floor steps only move upward. scoring.toml, score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (template-controlled, not task-editable). Function (0.6) carries more mass than polish+visual (0.4). (2) Gates cannot be failed by a stronger app: gates/render/judge.toml hro_gate_render needs wrong-password refusal then a seeded Recruiter sign-in with a usable workspace; gates/constraints/judge.toml hro_gate_shared needs a UI-created job (title, team, manager, 2 places) and candidate visible to the Observer (or another staff account) in an independent context with exactly one Applied card. Every element is a public requirement (instruction.md lines 3,11,17; hireops_rules.md sections 1-2). Both are all_pass binary with weight 1.0 and 0.0 reward mass. (3) Refusal rows cannot reward a dead feature: each carries a same-kind positive control, e.g. hro_interview_full ('the two cards that entered Interview are the control'), hro_bulk_all_or_none ('the successful multi-card moves in B are the control'), hro_undo_once ('The successful undos are the control'), hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff ('A candidate who cannot sign in ... makes this row 0'), hro_candidate_private ('A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'), hro_activity_refusals (successful lines as control); functional/prompt.md line 13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control' and line 17 ensures role replays carry fresh versions so a stale-version refusal is not credited as a role refusal. (4) Polish preservation rows score 0 when no live update arrives (polish judge.toml hro_pol_live_board / hro_pol_live_thread 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'), so a non-live app cannot outscore a live app on 'preserved focus'. Visual: gate failure gives raw Likert 1 normalized to 0 (visual/prompt.md line 12). Strict-but-public behaviours (401 anonymous, 403 role, 404 candidate not-found, Observer controls optional, hiding refused controls optional) are each in hireops_rules.md section 1/3/7, so a conforming stricter app is not penalised. (5) Weight concentration (computed with tomllib): functional 43 criteria sum 58.5, max row hro_stale_refused 2.5 -> 0.0256 reward; polish 5 rows sum 12 -> hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread 3 -> 0.05 each; visual 5 likert rows 1.2/6 -> 0.04 each. So a single polish or visual row outweighs any single functional row (~2x), and full visual spread (0.2) equals ~19.5 functional weight units (one third of functional). This is template-mandated dimension mass, not a demonstrated inversion: polish rows depend on working live updates and conversations, visual rows judge board/conversation surfaces that must exist, so a functionally weak app cannot readily reach top polish/visual. Recorded as a monitoring note per the workbook's internal annotation. ATTEMPTED COUNTEREXAMPLES. Broken app that might pass: a CRUD-only app (job + candidate create, persistence) clears both gates and the 0.05 floor (needs >2.925 functional units; hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_add_email_rules 1 + hro_restart 1.5 + hro_job_open 0.5 is possible), but polish rows are 0 without live board/threads and visual rows judge missing surfaces, so estimated reward (~0.04 functional + low visual) stays well below a functionally fuller app; no inversion constructed. Conforming app that could fail: an app keeping drafts server-side, using sockets for sends, or refusing in the UI before sending is explicitly accommodated (polish hro_pol_failed_send setOffline alternative; hro_refused_put_back 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes'; functional prompt line 23 replay when not offered). Remaining plausible inversion path, UNMEASURED: the 'NOT EXERCISED -> binary 0' budget rule (functional/prompt.md line 53) with a 9000 s functional timeout over 14 sequential protocols: a fully working app forces the judge through every step, so if budget runs out before V/A/D, late rows (hro_live_board 2.5, hro_activity 1, hro_restart 1.5) could be 0 for the better app while a worse app whose early steps fail fast may reach D and earn hro_restart. RUNTIME EVIDENCE. raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' All 6 indexed artifacts (workspace.cjs, results/workspace.json, server.log, board.png, conversation.png, candidate.png) hash-verify but are scripted golden observations, 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement.' REVIEW_POLICY.md requires hash-bound runtime records for reward discrimination and reward ordering (mutated weak apps vs golden through the configured judge) before clearance. None exists, so monotonicity is supported by design analysis only and cannot be upgraded to Pass.
